exposure: abnormal pelvic complaints (vaginal discharge, postcoital bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, dyspareunia, pelvic pain)
outcome: premaligant cervical lesions (atypical squamous cells of unknown significance, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion)
cohort: Female patients aged 25-70 years presenting with abnormal pelvic complaints with no uterine cause detected by ultrasonography, undergoing cervical Papanicolaou smear.
finding: Premalignant cervical lesions were found in 8.1% of symptomatic patients, highlighting the importance of early detection.
